About us

Transform SAP Data into Enterprise Intelligence.

Sria Infotech is a global SAP Data & AI transformation specialist. We help enterprises convert SAP transactional data into trusted business intelligence, predictive analytics, intelligent automation and AI-powered decisions.

Talk to our architects

SAP systems hold the most valuable data most enterprises own: every order, delivery, invoice, production confirmation and journal entry. Yet that data is often locked in complex structures, fragmented across instances and difficult to combine with the rest of the business.

We exist to close that gap. Our architects and engineers combine deep SAP data knowledge with modern cloud data platforms and enterprise AI — so that organisations can trust their numbers, see what is coming and act faster.

We work with SAP S/4HANA and ECC customers across manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, mining and metals, automotive, retail, FMCG and logistics.

What we do

  • ASAP Analytics
  • BCloud Data Engineering
  • CBusiness Intelligence
  • DAI Analytics
  • EEnterprise Data Architecture

Principles

How we work

  • Evidence over assertion

    We show the data lineage, the query and the reconciliation — and we expect our recommendations to be challenged.

  • Architecture with intent

    Every design decision is recorded with its rationale, alternatives and trade-offs.

  • Neutral advice

    Our recommendations follow your landscape and priorities, not a preferred vendor.

  • Lasting capability

    We measure success by what your teams can run and extend after we leave.

Skills

Describe a task once. Run it every time.

Skills combine a trigger, governed analysis steps and a follow-up — created in plain language, reviewed by people and versioned like code.

Skill: Month-end margin commentary

Described in plain language → compiled to a governed workflow

Trigger

Close day 3, 07:00

Or when gross margin moves more than 1 pt vs plan.

Actions

Analyse CO-PA variance

Decompose by price, volume, mix, FX; compare to plan and prior month.

Follow-up

Draft & route for approval

Commentary to the controller in Teams; publish to the board pack after approval.

“Every close, on day 3, explain the margin variance vs plan by region and product line, draft commentary and send it to the controller for approval.”

Works where you work

Bring SAP insights into the assistants you already use.

We expose governed SAP analytics through Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and APIs, so approved AI assistants, Microsoft Teams, Slack and SAP Joule can use the same certified metrics.

Your data stays yours

Enterprise-grade by design

  • Runs in your environment

    Built in your SAP and cloud tenants — your data does not leave your control.

  • No training on your data

    Enterprise AI services configured under terms that exclude training on your data.

  • SAP authorisations respected

    Every answer is filtered by the requesting user’s roles and row-level rules.

  • Private personal connections

    Personal mail, calendar and files stay private to each user; shared sources are governed.

  • Encrypted credentials

    Connector secrets live in your key vault, rotated and never exposed to models.

  • Complete audit trail

    Prompts, tool calls, sources and approvals are logged for compliance review.

For Finance, supply chain and operations leaders

Agentic Analytics

Agentic analytics goes beyond Q&A. Given a goal such as “why did margin drop?”, an agent plans the analysis, calls governed tools (semantic layer, queries, forecasts), decomposes drivers, tests hypotheses and returns evidence with a recommended next step — every step visible and auditable.

Try it live in AI StudioRequest a walkthrough

Agentic Analytics — investigation run

Illustrative demo · sample data
Goal: Why did gross margin drop?
  1. ✓Plan: scan trend → decompose → test cost vs price → recommend
  2. ✓Query semantic layer: gross margin by quarter
  3. ✓Detected largest drop: Q2 → Q3 (−4.4 pts)
  4. ✓Decompose by region and product line
  5. ✓Test: COGS +8.7% vs revenue +2.0%
  6. …Recommend: review material cost & pricing conditions

Δ gross margin by region (Q2 → Q3)

pts

  • South−8.2
  • West−4.1
  • East−3.5
  • North−3.3
  • Export−3.2

AI insight

Margin fell 4.4 pts, concentrated in South and Consumer products. Cost growth outpaced revenue — a cost-driven squeeze, not a volume issue.

Agent run · 7 tool calls · read-only · awaiting human review

Illustrative interface with fictional sample data. Not a live customer deployment.

Capabilities

What it does

  • Planning

    Breaks a business question into analytical sub-tasks.

  • Tool use

    Calls certified queries, decomposition, forecasting and anomaly tools through governed APIs.

  • Root-cause analysis

    Decomposes changes by region, product, customer, supplier or line, and tests price-versus-cost hypotheses.

  • Transparent trace

    Shows each step, query and intermediate result; actions require human approval.

Questions it answers

  • “Why did margin drop?”
  • “Investigate the OEE decline”
  • “What drove off-contract spend?”

  • CAPABILITY · 04

    Agentic Analytics

    Agentic analytics goes beyond Q&A. Given a goal such as “why did margin drop?”, an agent plans the analysis, calls governed tools (semantic layer, queries, forecasts), decomposes drivers, tests hypotheses and returns evidence with a recommended next step — every step visible and auditable.

    • Planning
    • Tool use
    • Root-cause analysis
    • Transparent trace
    Try it live Explore Agentic Analytics

    Goal: Why did gross margin drop?

    4. ✓Decompose by region and product line
    5. ✓Test: COGS +8.7% vs revenue +2.0%
    6. …Recommend: review material cost & pricing conditions

    pts

    • East−3.5

    • Export−3.2

    Margin fell 4.4 pts, concentrated in South and Consumer products. Cost growth outpaced revenue — a cost-driven squeeze, not a volume issue.

Responsible AI by design

Six controls built into every AI solution.

  • 01

    Grounded in governed data

    AI reads certified metrics and data products, never uncontrolled extracts.

  • 02

    Permission-aware

    Answers reflect the requesting user's SAP and platform authorisations.

  • 03

    Explainable

    Every answer shows its query, sources, definitions and data freshness.

  • 04

    Human in the loop

    Recommendations that change SAP data route through approval workflows.

  • 05

    Continuously evaluated

    Accuracy is measured against agreed business test sets before and after go-live.

  • 06

    Auditable

    Prompts, tool calls and outputs are logged for compliance review.

  • Speech processed by an enterprise speech service of your choice in production

Solution architecture portfolio

Eight reference architectures for SAP data and AI.

Each pattern is documented across source systems, integration, storage, transformation, semantics, BI and AI consumption, and governance — with guidance on when it fits.

  • 02

  • 04

    SAP + Snowflake + Cortex AI

    AI agents that analyse, explain and act on SAP data — under governance.

Which architecture fits?

ArchitectureBest fit when…Key considerations
01SAP BDC + Datasphere + SACSAP is the dominant source of business data · Finance and planning are primary consumers · Strategic commitment to SAP Business Technology PlatformLicence and capacity unit planning · Non-SAP data volume and variety · Skills in Datasphere modelling
02SAP + BigQuery + LookerGoogle Cloud is the strategic cloud · High-volume, blended SAP + digital data · Need for embedded analytics in customer-facing appsSAP extraction licensing · LookML development skills · Query cost governance
03SAP + Fabric + Power BIMicrosoft is the strategic platform · Large Power BI user base · Mixed SAP and Dynamics or Microsoft dataCapacity sizing (F SKUs) · SAP connector and gateway design · Workspace and domain governance
04SAP + Snowflake + Cortex AISnowflake is the enterprise data platform · Strong need for data sharing · AI use cases on structured and unstructured dataCDC tool selection and licensing · Credit consumption management · Semantic view design quality
05SAP + Databricks LakehouseStrong data science and engineering teams · High-volume operational / IoT data · ML is a core requirementEngineering skill depth · Cluster and serverless cost control · Semantic layer for business users
06SAP + Ontology + Decision IntelligenceComplex, interconnected operations · Need to close the loop from insight to action · Many systems describing the same business objectsOntology design and ownership · Write-back controls and SAP authorisations · Change management for decision processes
07SAP + Multi-Cloud AnalyticsMore than one strategic data platform · Multiple SAP instances or ERPs · Federated organisation structureGovernance overhead · Semantic consistency enforcement · Egress and duplication costs

Reference architecture 08

SAP + Agentic AI Analytics

A reference architecture for enterprise AI agents that query governed SAP data, reason over business context, call approved tools and hand decisions to people — with identity, guardrails and evaluation built in.

Discuss this architectureRead the whitepaper

Layer by layer

How the architecture works

01Source systems
  • SAP S/4HANA
  • SAP ECC
  • SAP BW / BW/4HANA
  • Documents, contracts, policies
02Integration
  • Governed data platform
  • SAP OData / CDS APIs
  • MCP servers & tool APIs
  • Document ingestion
03Data storage
  • Curated data products
  • Vector store
  • Agent memory & logs
04Transformation
  • Chunking & embeddings
  • Metadata enrichment
  • Evaluation datasets
05Semantic / context
  • Metrics & semantic layer
  • Knowledge graph / ontology
  • Business glossary & policies
06BI & AI consumption
  • Domain agents (CFO, procurement, supply)
  • Multi-agent orchestration
  • SAP Joule / Teams / Slack
  • Human approval steps

Security & governance

  • Identity propagation (user-level permissions)
  • Tool & action allow-lists
  • Prompt & output guardrails
  • Continuous evaluation
  • Complete audit trail

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • Analysis on demand

    Agents investigate variances and exceptions and return evidence, not just answers.

  • Permission-aware

    Agents see only what the requesting user is entitled to see.

  • Explainable

    Every answer shows the queries, sources and reasoning steps used.

  • Controlled action

    Proposed actions route through human approval before reaching SAP.

Appropriate use cases

  • Month-end variance investigation
  • Exception management in procure-to-pay
  • Inventory rebalancing recommendations
  • Executive Q&A over governed KPIs

Best fit when

  • Mature semantic layer or data products
  • Clear, repeatable analytical tasks
  • Appetite for controlled AI automation

Considerations

  • Evaluation and accuracy thresholds
  • Cost and latency management
  • Change management and trust building

Reference architecture 01

SAP Business Data Cloud + Datasphere + SAP Analytics Cloud

An SAP-first architecture for organisations that want harmonised SAP data products, a Datasphere business layer and SAC for analytics and planning — with the option to extend to Databricks or other platforms through zero-copy sharing.

Discuss this architectureRead the whitepaper

Layer by layer

How the architecture works

01Source systems
  • SAP S/4HANA (Cloud & Private)
  • SAP ECC
  • SAP SuccessFactors / Ariba
  • Non-SAP sources
02Integration
  • SAP-managed data products
  • Datasphere replication flows
  • BW data product generator
  • Remote tables (federation)
03Data storage
  • BDC object store
  • Datasphere spaces
  • HANA Cloud persistence
04Transformation
  • Transformation flows
  • Data flows & SQL views
  • Customer-managed data products
05Semantic / context
  • Analytic models
  • Business entities & hierarchies
  • Currency & unit conversion
06BI & AI consumption
  • SAC stories & planning
  • SAP Joule
  • Insight apps
  • Delta Sharing to Databricks

Security & governance

  • Space-level isolation
  • Data access controls (row-level)
  • Datasphere catalog & lineage
  • SAP Cloud Identity Services
  • Audit logging

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • Semantics retained

    SAP business context — hierarchies, currencies, fiscal calendars — is carried through without re-engineering.

  • Planning & actuals together

    SAC planning models run on the same governed data as reporting.

  • BW modernisation path

    Existing BW investments can be brought forward as data products rather than rebuilt.

  • Open by design

    Zero-copy sharing allows data science teams to use the same data products in Databricks.

Appropriate use cases

  • Group financial reporting and consolidation analytics
  • Integrated business planning
  • Working capital and cash analytics
  • BW/4HANA modernisation

Best fit when

  • SAP is the dominant source of business data
  • Finance and planning are primary consumers
  • Strategic commitment to SAP Business Technology Platform

Considerations

  • Licence and capacity unit planning
  • Non-SAP data volume and variety
  • Skills in Datasphere modelling

Reference architecture 02

SAP + Google BigQuery + Looker

Replicate SAP data into BigQuery, accelerate modelling with Google Cloud Cortex Framework, govern metrics in LookML and expose insight through Looker and Gemini-powered conversational analytics.

Discuss this architectureRead the whitepaper

Layer by layer

How the architecture works

01Source systems
  • SAP S/4HANA
  • SAP ECC
  • SAP BW / BW/4HANA
  • Google Ads, Salesforce, IoT
02Integration
  • SAP LT Replication Server + BigQuery Connector for SAP
  • Datasphere replication flows
  • Partner CDC tools
03Data storage
  • BigQuery raw / CDC datasets
  • Cloud Storage landing
  • BigLake tables
04Transformation
  • Cortex Framework data foundation
  • Dataform / dbt
  • Scheduled & materialised views
05Semantic / context
  • LookML models
  • Governed explores
  • Metric definitions
06BI & AI consumption
  • Looker dashboards
  • Conversational analytics (Gemini)
  • Vertex AI models
  • Embedded analytics

Security & governance

  • Dataplex catalog & quality
  • IAM & column-level security
  • Row-level access policies
  • VPC Service Controls
  • Cloud Audit Logs

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • Serverless scale

    BigQuery separates storage and compute, handling large SAP history without infrastructure management.

  • Accelerated SAP models

    Cortex Framework provides reference SAP data models for order-to-cash, procure-to-pay and more.

  • Governed metrics

    LookML defines KPIs once; every dashboard and AI answer uses the same logic.

  • Blended data

    SAP data combined with marketing, web and IoT data already in Google Cloud.

Appropriate use cases

  • Demand sensing with external signals
  • Customer 360 combining SAP SD and marketing data
  • Supply chain control tower
  • Sustainability and emissions analytics

Best fit when

  • Google Cloud is the strategic cloud
  • High-volume, blended SAP + digital data
  • Need for embedded analytics in customer-facing apps

Considerations

  • SAP extraction licensing
  • LookML development skills
  • Query cost governance

01Source systems

  • SAP ECC

02Integration

  • Lakeflow Connect
  • Partner CDC
  • Auto Loader
03Data storage
  • Delta Lake bronze
  • Silver conformed
  • Gold data products

  • Lakeflow declarative pipelines

  • Feature engineering

  • Unity Catalog metric views
  • Feature store
  • Vector search indexes

  • Power BI / Tableau

Security & governance

  • Attribute-based access control
  • Lineage & audit
  • Lakehouse monitoring
  • Model governance (MLflow)

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • One platform for data & AI

    Engineering, analytics and machine learning share the same governed data.

  • Open formats

    Delta Lake and Delta Sharing avoid proprietary lock-in.

  • Advanced ML

    Forecasting, optimisation and deep learning on SAP and operational data.

  • SAP partnership path

    Zero-copy sharing of SAP data products into Databricks via SAP Business Data Cloud.

Appropriate use cases

  • Predictive maintenance with SAP PM + sensor data
  • Yield and quality analytics

  • High-volume operational / IoT data

Reference architecture 07

SAP + Multi-Cloud Analytics

For enterprises operating more than one data platform — through acquisitions, regional choices or workload fit — this architecture keeps SAP semantics consistent and governed while letting each domain use the platform that suits it.

Discuss this architectureRead the whitepaper

Layer by layer

How the architecture works

01Source systems
  • Multiple SAP instances
  • Regional ERPs
  • SaaS applications
02Integration
  • SAP data products
  • Zero-copy sharing
  • CDC per platform
  • Federated query
03Data storage
  • Domain-owned platforms
  • Open table formats (Iceberg / Delta)
  • Shared reference data
04Transformation
  • Shared SAP model library
  • Platform-native pipelines
  • Data contracts
05Semantic / context
  • Universal metric definitions
  • Federated business glossary
  • Cross-platform semantic layer
06BI & AI consumption
  • Tool of choice per domain
  • Group consolidated views
  • Cross-platform AI agents

Security & governance

  • Federated catalog & lineage
  • Policy-as-code across platforms
  • Data residency controls
  • Data product ownership (mesh)
  • Cost allocation

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • Choice without chaos

    Domains choose platforms; the enterprise keeps one set of definitions.

  • M&A friendly

    Integrate acquired businesses without forced re-platforming.

  • Residency compliance

    Data stays in-region while group reporting remains possible.

  • Workload fit

    Each workload runs where it performs and costs best.

Appropriate use cases

  • Post-merger integration analytics
  • Regional data residency with group reporting
  • Shared services across business units
  • Data mesh operating models

Best fit when

  • More than one strategic data platform
  • Multiple SAP instances or ERPs
  • Federated organisation structure

Considerations

  • Governance overhead
  • Semantic consistency enforcement
  • Egress and duplication costs

SAP + Enterprise Ontology + Decision Intelligence

Build a business ontology over SAP and non-SAP data — customers, materials, plants, orders, suppliers and their relationships — and use it to power scenario simulation, decision apps and governed write-back to SAP.

Layer by layer

How the architecture works

01Source systems
  • SAP S/4HANA
  • SAP ECC
  • SAP BW / BW/4HANA
  • MES, CRM, WMS, external risk feeds
02Integration
  • CDC into data platform
  • SAP OData / CDS APIs
  • Event streams
03Data storage
  • Lakehouse / warehouse
  • Graph store
  • Time-series store
04Transformation
  • Entity resolution
  • Relationship extraction
  • Object materialisation
05Semantic / context
  • Business ontology (objects, links, actions)
  • Business rules
  • Metric & KPI layer
06BI & AI consumption
  • Decision apps & what-if
  • Graph-aware AI copilots
  • Approved write-back to SAP
  • Operational dashboards

Security & governance

  • Object-level permissions
  • Action approval workflows
  • Ontology versioning
  • Full decision audit trail
  • Data stewardship

Business benefits

Why organisations choose this pattern

  • Shared language

    One model of the business that operations, finance and AI all understand.

  • From insight to action

    Decisions are captured and executed through governed actions, not spreadsheets.

  • Impact analysis

    Trace how a supplier delay propagates to orders, customers and revenue.

  • Better AI grounding

    Relationships give language models the context to reason correctly.

Appropriate use cases

  • Supply disruption impact and mitigation
  • Order promising and allocation
  • Multi-plant production planning scenarios
  • Customer service risk triage

Best fit when

  • Complex, interconnected operations
  • Need to close the loop from insight to action
  • Many systems describing the same business objects

Considerations

  • Ontology design and ownership
  • Write-back controls and SAP authorisations

Engagement blueprints

Our approach to six common challenges

Illustrative blueprints describing how we typically structure engagements. They are not client case studies and contain no client results.

  • ManufacturingBlueprint 01

    BW modernisation to SAP Business Data Cloud

    Challenge: A large SAP BW estate with overlapping reports, slow change cycles and growing licence cost.

    Approach

    1. 1Usage-led inventory of queries, flows and users
    2. 2Target landscape on BDC, Datasphere and SAC
    3. 3Domain-by-domain migration with automated reconciliation
    4. 4Decommissioning plan for unused content

    What success looks like

    • Certified reporting catalogue per domain
    • Reconciled figures against SAP for every migrated model
    • Retired legacy objects with an audit trail
    Architecture 01: SAP BDC + Datasphere + SAC
  • PharmaceuticalsBlueprint 02

    Batch & quality analytics on a governed lakehouse

    Challenge: Batch, deviation and release data spread across SAP, LIMS and spreadsheets slows release decisions.

    Approach

    1. 1Batch genealogy model across SAP QM, PP-PI and LIMS
    2. 2Validated, version-controlled pipelines
    3. 3Release-cycle and deviation dashboards
    4. 4Predictive release-time model with explainability

    What success looks like

    • One batch view from material to release
    • Traceable lineage suitable for validation
    • Earlier visibility of release bottlenecks
    Architecture 05: SAP + Databricks Lakehouse
  • Retail / FMCGBlueprint 03

    Conversational analytics over SAP sales data

    Challenge: Commercial teams wait days for ad-hoc analysis; KPI definitions differ between regions.

    Approach

    1. 1Certified semantic model for revenue, margin and trade spend
    2. 2Evaluation set of real business questions
    3. 3Copilot in Teams and the web with query transparency
    4. 4Adoption programme by role

    What success looks like

    • Agreed KPI definitions across regions
    • Answers that show query, source and freshness
    • Measured accuracy against an evaluation set
    Architecture 08: SAP + Agentic AI Analytics
  • Mining & MetalsBlueprint 04

    Asset performance and cost-per-tonne analytics

    Challenge: Maintenance, production and cost data are reconciled manually across remote sites.

    Approach

    1. 1Asset and work-order model from SAP PM
    2. 2Telemetry ingestion and failure-mode features
    3. 3Cost-per-tonne driver analysis
    4. 4Site-level operational dashboards

    What success looks like

    • Single asset-health view per site
    • Explained cost-per-tonne movements
    • Early-warning signals for critical assets
    Architecture 05: SAP + Databricks Lakehouse
  • AutomotiveBlueprint 05

    Supplier risk & shortage impact with an enterprise ontology

    Challenge: Part shortages surface late and their impact on vehicles and orders is unclear.

    Approach

    1. 1Ontology linking parts, suppliers, BOMs, orders and vehicles
    2. 2External risk signals joined to supplier performance
    3. 3Shortage impact simulation
    4. 4Approval-based mitigation actions

    What success looks like

    • Impact of a shortage traceable to orders in minutes
    • Prioritised supplier watchlist
    • Decisions captured with an audit trail
    Architecture 06: SAP + Ontology + Decision Intelligence
  • LogisticsBlueprint 06

    Control-tower analytics with an exception agent

    Challenge: Exceptions across carriers and warehouses are handled reactively by email.

    Approach

    1. 1OTIF and freight cost model from SAP TM/EWM
    2. 2Delay prediction on shipment events
    3. 3Agent that triages exceptions and drafts responses
    4. 4Human approval before customer communication

    What success looks like

    • Exceptions prioritised by impact
    • Consistent, auditable responses
    • Freight-audit anomalies flagged automatically
    Architecture 08: SAP + Agentic AI Analytics

Built for global SAP landscapes

Many SAP instances. Many regions. One intelligence layer.

Global enterprises run multiple SAP systems across regions and clouds. We design architectures that harmonise them into consistent, governed metrics — while respecting data residency.

  • Multi-instance harmonisation

    Conform company codes, charts of accounts, currencies and material masters across SAP instances.

  • Region-aware data placement

    Keep data in-region where required, with group-level reporting on governed aggregates.

  • Multi-cloud by design

    SAP Business Data Cloud alongside Snowflake, Databricks, Fabric or BigQuery — one semantic layer.

Globe is illustrative: arcs depict data moving between cloud regions.

Your data stays yours

Enterprise-grade security and governance, by design.

  • Runs in your environment

    Built in your SAP and cloud tenants — your data does not leave your control.

  • No training on your data

    Enterprise AI services configured under terms that exclude training on your data.

  • SAP authorisations respected

    Every answer is filtered by the requesting user’s roles and row-level rules.

  • Private personal connections

    Personal mail, calendar and files stay private to each user; shared sources are governed.

  • Encrypted credentials

    Connector secrets live in your key vault, rotated and never exposed to models.

  • Complete audit trail

    Prompts, tool calls, sources and approvals are logged for compliance review.

FAQ

Questions clients ask us.

Can’t find your answer? Ask an architect →

  • What does Sria Infotech do?+

    We help enterprises turn SAP data into trusted analytics and AI: SAP Business Data Cloud, Datasphere and SAC; cloud data engineering on BigQuery, Snowflake, Fabric and Databricks; BI; and governed AI analysts and agents.

  • Do you only work with SAP data?+

    SAP is our specialism, but most programmes combine SAP with CRM, MES, IoT, files and SaaS data. Our architectures are designed for blended SAP and non-SAP data.

  • Which AI models and platforms do you support?+

    We are model-agnostic. We design solutions for the models and platforms you approve — including enterprise offerings from major AI providers, open-weight models and SAP’s own generative AI services — and route each task to the most suitable one.

  • Where does our data live?+

    In your environment. We build in your SAP and cloud tenants, keep credentials in your key vault, respect your SAP authorisations and configure enterprise AI services so your data is not used to train models.

  • Can AI agents change data in SAP?+

    Only if you choose, and only through approved workflows. By default our agents are read-only analysts; any proposed action routes to a person for approval and is fully audited.

  • How do we get started?+

    Take the free readiness self-assessment, then book a working session with our architects. Most clients start with a short assessment followed by a fixed-scope pilot on one business domain.

  • Will this replace SAP Analytics Cloud or Power BI?+

    No. We make your existing BI tools more valuable by giving them governed semantics, and add conversational and agentic experiences where they help.

Agentic AI · 7 min read

Governing AI agents that work with SAP data

Agents that query data and propose actions need identity, permissions, evaluation and approval controls designed in from day one.

Published 23 June 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

An AI agent that reads SAP data and proposes actions is effectively a new kind of user. It should be governed like one.

Five controls

  • Identity propagation: the agent acts with the requesting user's permissions
  • Tool allow-lists: explicit, minimal set of queries and APIs
  • Human approval for any change to transactional systems
  • Continuous evaluation against agreed test sets
  • Full audit trail of prompts, tool calls and outputs

Start with analysis, then action

The safest path is to deploy agents first as analysts — investigating, explaining and recommending — and only later allow controlled actions with approval workflows.

SAP Analytics · 6 min read

SAP BW modernization: four paths and how to choose

Lift, bridge, rebuild or retire. A pragmatic look at modernisation options for BW 7.x and BW/4HANA estates.

Published 12 May 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

The four paths

  • Bridge: carry BW content forward into the SAP Business Data Cloud landscape
  • Rebuild: redesign priority models natively in Datasphere or a cloud platform
  • Coexist: keep BW for stable reporting while new use cases go cloud-native
  • Retire: decommission unused content identified through usage analysis

Start with usage

Long-lived BW estates often accumulate queries and data flows that are rarely used. A usage-led inventory shows what matters before any migration effort is committed.

Cloud Data Engineering · 9 min read

Choosing a cloud data platform for SAP data: a decision framework

BigQuery, Snowflake, Fabric, Databricks or SAP Business Data Cloud? The right answer depends on five factors — not on a feature checklist.

Published 18 August 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

Every major data platform now has an SAP story. Choosing between them on features alone rarely leads to a good outcome. We use five factors.

Five factors

  • Share of SAP versus non-SAP data in priority use cases
  • Strategic cloud and productivity-suite alignment
  • Primary consumers: finance and planning, BI users, or data scientists
  • Existing skills and operating model
  • Data sharing needs across business units and partners

Coexistence is normal

Many enterprises end up with an SAP-native layer for finance and planning and a cloud platform for blended, high-volume and AI workloads. The goal is consistent semantics across both, not a single platform at any cost.

Data Architecture · 8 min read

Applying medallion architecture to SAP data — without losing the plot

Bronze, silver, gold is simple on a slide. With SAP's table structures, deltas and conversions, each layer needs specific rules.

Published 14 July 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

Bronze: preserve fidelity

Land SAP data as close to source as possible, including change records and technical fields. This is your audit and replay layer.

Silver: conform and decode

Apply delta merges, decode technical keys, join texts, and standardise currencies and units. Keep SAP keys so figures can be reconciled.

Gold: business data products

Model around business processes — order-to-cash, procure-to-pay, plan-to-produce — with owners, contracts and documented metrics.

Common pitfalls

  • Skipping reconciliation to SAP totals
  • Rebuilding SAP logic differently in every gold model
  • Ignoring fiscal-period and currency-translation rules

SAP Analytics · 7 min read

SAP Business Data Cloud: what actually changes for your data architecture

Data products, zero-copy sharing and a new place for BW. A practical view of where SAP Business Data Cloud fits and the decisions it forces.

Published 20 October 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

For most SAP customers, the analytics question has never been whether SAP data matters — it is where to model it, who owns it and how to keep its business meaning intact once it leaves the ERP. SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC) reframes that question around data products.

From extracts to data products

Instead of every team building its own extracts, BDC introduces SAP-managed data products: curated, documented datasets with business semantics attached. Customer-managed data products extend the same idea to your own models.

The practical effect is that the unit of delivery becomes a product with an owner and a contract, not a pipeline.

Decisions to make early

  • Which domains rely on SAP-managed data products versus custom models
  • Where BW content moves — into BDC, into Datasphere, or is retired
  • Which workloads need sharing into Databricks or other platforms
  • How security and access policies are defined once and enforced everywhere

Our view

BDC is strongest where SAP is the dominant source and finance or planning are primary consumers. Where non-SAP data dominates, it works best as the SAP semantic hub within a wider platform strategy rather than as the only platform.

AI Analytics · 6 min read

Why your semantic layer matters more than your LLM

Conversational analytics fails quietly when models guess what 'revenue' means. Governed semantics are the foundation for trustworthy AI answers.

Published 29 September 2026 · Sria Infotech Architecture Team

Ask five people in a company what net revenue means and you may get five answers. Ask a large language model and it will confidently pick one. That is the core risk of conversational analytics on enterprise data.

What the model needs

  • Certified metric definitions with calculation logic
  • Business-friendly names, synonyms and descriptions
  • Hierarchies, fiscal calendars and currency rules
  • Row- and column-level security that follows the user

Show the working

Every AI-generated answer should show the query it ran, the metrics it used and the freshness of the data. That transparency builds trust faster than any accuracy claim.

Evaluation sets — real business questions with agreed answers — should be built before go-live and run continuously afterwards.

  • B.6

    Lakehouse & warehouse

    Raw, conformed and curated layers, partitioning, clustering and cost-aware storage design.

  • B.7

    ETL / ELT pipelines

    Orchestrated, tested, version-controlled transformations with data contracts and lineage.

Intended outcomes

What changes for the business

  • SAP data available alongside non-SAP data in your chosen cloud platform
  • Delta-aware pipelines with reconciliation back to the SAP source
  • Reusable SAP data models instead of one-off extracts
  • Operational runbooks, monitoring and cost visibility

Outcomes describe programme objectives; results depend on each organisation’s context.

Hello! I’m your AI Studio assistant and I’m happy to help. Type or speak a request and I’ll build the dashboard instantly. Try “create a procurement dashboard”, “show margin by product line” or “why did margin drop?”.
Voice & text commands

You can type or say things like: • "Create a CFO / sales / procurement / inventory / manufacturing dashboard" • "Show spend by category", "Top 5 customers by revenue as a table", "OEE trend" • "Why did margin drop in Q3?" — runs a multi-step agentic investigation • "Read the dashboard", "Read chart 2", "Next chart", "Previous chart" • "Make chart 2 a line chart", "Remove chart 4", "Filter to the West region", "Clear filter" • "Switch to light theme", "Go to the architectures page", "Stop"

Demo notes: data is fictional. In this demo, language understanding is rule-based and runs locally; production deployments use an LLM grounded in your governed semantic layer. Voice input uses your browser’s speech recognition (Chrome, Edge, Safari) and needs microphone permission — some browsers process speech in the vendor’s cloud. Enterprise deployments can use a speech service of your choice.

Design principles

How we design visual analytics

  • Answer a question

    Every visual starts from a business question, not a chart type.

  • One definition per metric

    Charts read from the certified semantic layer, never from ad-hoc extracts.

  • Motion with meaning

    Animation shows flow, change and causality — and respects reduced-motion settings.

  • Accessible by default

    Text alternatives, keyboard focus, colour-safe palettes and voice narration.

Sria Infotech · Architecture whitepaper 08

SAP + Agentic AI Analytics

AI agents that analyse, explain and act on SAP data — under governance.

Transform SAP Data into Enterprise Intelligence.

01Executive summary

A reference architecture for enterprise AI agents that query governed SAP data, reason over business context, call approved tools and hand decisions to people — with identity, guardrails and evaluation built in.

Core platforms: LLM platform of choice, Semantic layer, Agent orchestration.

02Reference architecture

01Source systemsSAP S/4HANA · SAP ECC · SAP BW / BW/4HANA · Documents, contracts, policies
02IntegrationGoverned data platform · SAP OData / CDS APIs · MCP servers & tool APIs · Document ingestion
03Data storageCurated data products · Vector store · Agent memory & logs
04TransformationChunking & embeddings · Metadata enrichment · Evaluation datasets
05Semantic / contextMetrics & semantic layer · Knowledge graph / ontology · Business glossary & policies
06BI & AI consumptionDomain agents (CFO, procurement, supply) · Multi-agent orchestration · SAP Joule / Teams / Slack · Human approval steps
Security & governanceIdentity propagation (user-level permissions) · Tool & action allow-lists · Prompt & output guardrails · Continuous evaluation · Complete audit trail

03Business benefits

  • Analysis on demand. Agents investigate variances and exceptions and return evidence, not just answers.
  • Permission-aware. Agents see only what the requesting user is entitled to see.
  • Explainable. Every answer shows the queries, sources and reasoning steps used.
  • Controlled action. Proposed actions route through human approval before reaching SAP.

04Appropriate use cases

  • Month-end variance investigation
  • Exception management in procure-to-pay
  • Inventory rebalancing recommendations
  • Executive Q&A over governed KPIs

05Decision criteria

Best fit when

  • Mature semantic layer or data products
  • Clear, repeatable analytical tasks
  • Appetite for controlled AI automation

Considerations

  • Evaluation and accuracy thresholds
  • Cost and latency management
  • Change management and trust building

06Implementation approach

  1. Assess — SAP landscape, data domains, consumers and constraints.
  2. Design — target architecture, security model and data product boundaries.
  3. Pilot — one business domain end to end, reconciled to SAP.
  4. Scale — additional domains, self-service enablement and AI use cases.
  5. Operate — monitoring, cost management, governance cadence.

SAP + Multi-Cloud Analytics

Consistent SAP semantics across clouds, regions and business units.

Transform SAP Data into Enterprise Intelligence.

01Executive summary

For enterprises operating more than one data platform — through acquisitions, regional choices or workload fit — this architecture keeps SAP semantics consistent and governed while letting each domain use the platform that suits it.

Core platforms: SAP Datasphere, Snowflake / Databricks / BigQuery / Fabric, Federated catalog.

02Reference architecture

01Source systemsMultiple SAP instances · Regional ERPs · SaaS applications
02IntegrationSAP data products · Zero-copy sharing · CDC per platform · Federated query

04TransformationShared SAP model library · Platform-native pipelines · Data contracts
05Semantic / contextUniversal metric definitions · Federated business glossary · Cross-platform semantic layer
06BI & AI consumptionTool of choice per domain · Group consolidated views · Cross-platform AI agents
Security & governanceFederated catalog & lineage · Policy-as-code across platforms · Data residency controls · Data product ownership (mesh) · Cost allocation

03Business benefits

  • Choice without chaos. Domains choose platforms; the enterprise keeps one set of definitions.
  • M&A friendly. Integrate acquired businesses without forced re-platforming.
  • Residency compliance. Data stays in-region while group reporting remains possible.
  • Workload fit. Each workload runs where it performs and costs best.

  • Regional data residency with group reporting
  • Shared services across business units
  • Data mesh operating models

Best fit when

  • Multiple SAP instances or ERPs
  • Federated organisation structure

Considerations

  • Governance overhead
  • Semantic consistency enforcement
  • Egress and duplication costs

SAP + Snowflake + Cortex AI

Governed SAP data in the AI Data Cloud, with LLM-powered analytics in place.

Transform SAP Data into Enterprise Intelligence.

01Executive summary

Replicate SAP data into Snowflake, model it with dynamic tables or dbt, define semantic views for Cortex Analyst and build AI applications and agents without moving data out of the governance boundary.

02Reference architecture

01Source systemsSAP S/4HANA · SAP ECC · SAP BW / BW/4HANA · Marketplace & partner data

03Data storageRaw SAP schemas · Apache Iceberg tables · Curated data marts
04TransformationDynamic tables · dbt projects · Snowpark (Python)
05Semantic / contextSemantic views · Cortex Search indexes · Business glossary & tags
06BI & AI consumptionCortex Analyst (text-to-SQL) · Cortex Agents · Streamlit apps · Power BI / Tableau / Sigma
Security & governanceSnowflake Horizon catalog · Masking & row access policies · Object tagging & classification · Role-based access control · Access history & lineage

03Business benefits

  • AI inside the boundary. LLM functions run where the data lives, respecting existing roles and policies.
  • Secure collaboration. Data sharing across business units, subsidiaries and partners without copies.
  • Elastic workloads. Separate warehouses for ingestion, transformation, BI and AI.
  • Open formats. Iceberg tables keep options open for other engines.

04Appropriate use cases

  • Conversational finance analytics
  • Supplier and spend intelligence
  • Cross-subsidiary data sharing
  • Document + data AI (contracts, invoices)

Best fit when

  • Snowflake is the enterprise data platform
  • Strong need for data sharing
  • AI use cases on structured and unstructured data

  • CDC tool selection and licensing

  • Semantic view design quality
